c.tagline: A living Jiangnan water town of black-awning boats, arched stone bridges, rice wine and the hometown of writer Lu Xun.

taxi.fareNote: Metered street taxis are common, but Didi is easier for foreigners; the old-city canal quarters around Lu Xun's hometown are largely pedestrian, so cars drop you at the edges.

emergency.note: 120 is the ambulance number, 119 is fire and 110 is police. English is limited outside big hotels, so keep addresses written in Chinese and a translation app handy.

hood_desc: The historic core of Shaoxing, threaded with canals, arched stone bridges and black-awning wu peng chuan boats, and home to the hugely popular Lu Xun Native Place, Shen Garden and the Xianheng Tavern of his stories; the essential, walkable base steeped in Jiangnan atmosphere.

A beautifully restored Ming and Qing canal street of whitewashed houses, teahouses and small workshops running beside the water, anchored by the elegant eight-character Bazi Bridge nearby; a quieter, photogenic slice of old Shaoxing a short walk from Lu Xun's hometown.

The modern northern district built around the enormous China Textile City and the dramatic quarried cliffs and green pools of Keyan Scenic Area; a business-focused base with newer hotels, well linked to Hangzhou by metro and high-speed rail.

A scenic area a few kilometres east where sheer stone cliffs left by ancient quarrying rise straight from a jade-green lake, explored by narrow flat-bottomed boats; a calm, nature-leaning spot away from the city bustle.

The riverside district on the east bank of the Cao'e River, home to celadon heritage and the family roots of many overseas Chinese; a spread-out, residential base with international-brand hotels and easy links back to the old city.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water, as locals do.

transit.hours: Metro trains run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM; city buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 9:30 PM, after which Didi and taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Shaoxing Rail Transit runs a growing metro network (Lines 1 and 2) that links the high-speed station, the old city and Keqiao, and connects into Hangzhou's metro; an extensive city bus system covers the rest, alongside Didi and taxis.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning a QR code in Alipay, WeChat Pay or the metro app, tap a rechargeable transit card, or use exact-change cash on buses; fares are distance-based, typically a few yuan.

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels.

landmarks: Lu Xun Native Place
A beautifully preserved historic quarter of whitewashed houses and canals celebrating China's greatest modern writer, including his family home, study and the Sanwei Study.
Shen Garden (Shenyuan)
A romantic Song-dynasty garden immortalised by poet Lu You's heartbroken verses to his lost love Tang Wan, inscribed on its walls.
East Lake (Dong Hu)
A dramatic lake beneath sheer chiselled cliffs left by ancient quarrying, best explored by black-awning wupeng boat through rock tunnels.
Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)
The bamboo-shaded site where calligrapher Wang Xizhi composed his legendary Orchid Pavilion Preface in 353 AD, a pilgrimage place for calligraphy lovers.
Mausoleum of Yu the Great (Dayu Ling)
A solemn temple and tomb complex at the foot of Kuaiji Mountain honouring China's legendary flood-taming founder of the Xia dynasty.
Cangqiao Straight Street
Shaoxing's most atmospheric canal-side historic street, lined with stone bridges, wine shops and centuries-old houses draped over the water.
Bazi Bridge
A rare surviving Song-dynasty stone bridge shaped like the character for eight, gracefully spanning a quiet canal since 1256.
Zhou Enlai Ancestral Home
The elegant ancestral residence of China's beloved first premier, a courtyard complex telling the Zhou family story in the old town.
Yingtian Pagoda and Tashan Hill
A slender ancient pagoda crowning a wooded city-centre hill, offering rooftop views across Shaoxing's canals and tiled roofs.
Shaoxing Museum
A free comprehensive museum tracing the ancient Yue kingdom and Shaoxing's history through bronze daggers, ceramics, and a millennia-spanning historical exhibition.

train.note: Shaoxing has no international trains. From Shaoxing North Railway Station, frequent high-speed trains reach Hangzhou in about 18-25 minutes, Ningbo in around 30-40 minutes and Shanghai Hongqiao in about 1.5 hours, putting the whole Yangtze Delta within easy reach. The older Shaoxing Station in the city handles some conventional services, and Shaoxing East serves the eastern districts. Book on 12306 with your passport; trains on this corridor run every few minutes so there is rarely any need to plan far ahead.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Shaoxing. Long-distance buses from the Shaoxing bus stations run to Hangzhou (about 1 hour), Ningbo, Zhuji and the Buddhist sights around Xinchang and Shengzhou, though the high-speed train is usually faster. Counter sales with ID are the norm, and for Hangzhou the frequent trains and the intercity metro link make the coach largely redundant.

ferry.note: Shaoxing is famous for its canals and the small black-awning boats poled through the old town, but these are sightseeing and local hire craft rather than transport; there is no scheduled passenger ferry to anywhere, and the city is about 30 km inland from Hangzhou Bay.

half.name: Anchang Ancient Town
half.blurb: A quieter, less commercialised canal town about 15 km northwest, famous for its long covered waterside walkway, arched bridges and dangling cured sausages and soy sauce made the traditional way.

half.name: Yellow Wine Town (Huangjiu Xiaozhen)
half.blurb: The heartland of Shaoxing's amber rice wine, where you can tour the huge earthenware jars of a working huangjiu cellar, taste the region's signature drink and see it used in local cooking.

half.name: Keyan Scenic Area
half.blurb: A striking landscape of sheer cliffs and pools left by 1,500 years of stone quarrying in Keqiao, with the improbably balanced Rocket Rock and a giant cliff-carved Maitreya Buddha.

full.name: Hangzhou & West Lake
full.blurb: Zhejiang's celebrated capital, whose willow-lined West Lake, tea hills and pagodas are barely 20 minutes away by high-speed train - an easy and rewarding full-day escape.

full.name: Xinchang Great Buddha Temple
full.blurb: A 1,600-year-old cliffside temple south of Shaoxing built around a colossal seated Maitreya carved into the rock, set among bamboo and tea country.

full.name: Ningbo
full.blurb: A historic port city about 40 minutes east by train, home to the ancient Tianyi Ge library, the restored Old Bund and gateway to the Buddhist island of Putuoshan.
